_comment: Aelgard Wilds bestiary. PvP-enabled frontier region. Monsters here are tuned for coexistence with hostile players — many are revenant-tag (retain gear after death), some are chaos-corrupted variants. Tone: raw, dangerous, unregulated. Risk/reward.
_region_tone: windburn, long sightlines, everyone armed, nobody civil. Law ends at the Black-Stone Wall. Creatures here fight dirty because the rules allow it.

monsters.name: Revenant knight
monsters.examine: A ghostly knight. Keeps gear the living abandoned.
bible: Revenant knights are the ghost-echoes of knights who died in the Wilds and whose bodies were not recovered. Their gear, preserved in undeath, is higher-quality than any living player's casual kit.

They drop gear rarely — and what they drop is a mix of weapons, amulets, and armour that includes items no longer craftable in any living Aelgard forge. These are the 'ancient' tier of revenant-exclusive items.
They fight with ranging magic, switch to melee only if cornered. Best engaged with a single heavy burst rather than prolonged exchange.
monsters.habitat: the Wilds interior, the Forgotten Ride, deep-wilds level 30+
monsters.reagent_callout: Ancient emblem (1/32, Wilds-unique) — tradable to the Revenant Exchange for ancient-tier items.

monsters.name: Revenant dragon
monsters.examine: The ghost of a dragon that died in the Wilds. Still carrying grudges.
bible: Revenant dragons are the rarest and deepest-Wilds revenants. Five are known to exist, and their territories are fixed. They patrol larger ranges than living dragons — one revenant dragon covers an area that would normally host four living ones.
They breathe ghost-fire, which ignores dragonhide defence and drains prayer-points instead. Carrying extra prayer potions is standard.
Their loot pool includes the rarest revenant items — specifically, the ancient hilt, the ancient vestige, and the notorious ancient crystal.
monsters.habitat: five fixed patrol-territories across deep-wilds level 40+
monsters.reagent_callout: Ancient crystal (1/512 collection-log) — reagent for the endgame Wilds weapon 'Voidwaker'.

monsters.name: Chaos elemental
monsters.examine: An entity of pure chaos. Unpredictable attacks.
bible: The Chaos elemental is a Wilds singular boss — not a species. One exists. It occupies a fixed lair in the eastern deep-wilds and is the culmination of the Wilds' chaos-domain magic accreting into form over centuries.

Its attack pattern is literally unpredictable — each tick it selects a different attack style at random. The player cannot pray against its attacks; only high armor-coverage across multiple defence types works.
Killing it is a formal in-game event; defeats are announced across the server. The Wilds fishermen have a tradition of naming their next catch after the killer.
monsters.reagent_callout: Dragon 2h sword (1/256 from chaos elemental) — endgame crush weapon, classic wilderness unique.

monsters.name: Lava dragon
monsters.examine: A dragon wreathed in lava. Deep wilderness only.
bible: Lava dragons inhabit the Wilds' lava isles — a series of volcanic islets in the deep-western wilderness. They are the hottest dragon species; their hide exceeds 1200 degrees at rest.
They cannot be attacked in melee without thermal gear. A player without appropriate fire-resistance will take damage from proximity alone.
Their bones, rare drops, are the only dragon-bones that maintain heat indefinitely. Lava-dragon bones buried in a forge raise its peak temperature by 300 degrees — a sought-after smithing upgrade.
monsters.reagent_callout: Lava dragon bones (always drop) — buried into forge for a permanent +300C smithing station upgrade.

monsters.name: Black-stone warden
monsters.examine: Guardian of the Black-Stone Wall. Its patrol is the edge of law.
bible: The Black-Stone warden is a Wilds capstone boss. Two exist: they patrol the outer perimeter of the Black-Stone Wall, which nominally separates the Wilds from civilised regions. They are arguably the last lawful defense on the Wilds side.
A warden does not enter the Wilds interior and does not leave the Wall. Engagement is a choice by the player — walk to the Wall, accept combat.
Their loot includes a warden-seal, which is the only item that can open the Black-Stone's hidden gate to the Crown's emergency-evacuation quarter.
monsters.habitat: the Black-Stone Wall perimeter, two fixed patrol arcs
monsters.reagent_callout: Warden-seal (1/1 per warden, respawn 30 min) — key to Black-Stone hidden gate (lore content).

monsters.name: Rogue magus
monsters.examine: A mage who fled a guild investigation. Now Wilds-caste.
bible: Rogue magi are disgraced magic-caste adventurers from the Heartlands, Moryskah, or Veilwood who fled to the Wilds to avoid guild prosecution. Most are wanted; some are violent; all are skilled.
A rogue magus fights with the spellbook of his former guild. Identifying the book in combat tells the player where the rogue is from and, often, why he fled.
They drop partially-used spellbooks — salvageable for the partial-unknown spells within. Each magus has a different book; there is a collection log.
monsters.habitat: Wilds caves, abandoned towers, hidden magus-camps
monsters.reagent_callout: Partial spellbook (variable drop) — 9 unique spellbook fragments (1 per magus-origin guild) complete the Wilds Spellbook collection.

monsters.name: Bone thrower
monsters.examine: Throws bones. You were expecting stones.
bible: Bone throwers are Wilds skeletons who picked up the throwing-game from the Moryskah fenbolters and adapted. They range farther than a fenbolter (up to 55 paces) and carry a larger stockpile of bone-ammunition, usually 20-30 bones.
They are territorial about their throwing-circle — a paced-out area of loose bone-scatter that they defend.
Killed, they drop a mix of rune-tier weapons (from players they've downed) and bone-weapon variants that are slightly better than their Moryskah equivalents.
monsters.habitat: Wilds open ground, specifically the Bone-Scatter Fields
monsters.reagent_callout: Wilderness bone (1/20) — reagent for the wilderness bone-throwing spear (niche vs armoured-tag).

monsters.name: Venom spider
monsters.examine: A spider the size of a horse. Venomous. Hungry.
bible: Venom spiders are Wilds wilderness bosses native to the Spider's Nest, a mid-deep wilderness territory. They are not a species in the natural-history sense; only one exists at a time. A Wilds hunter killing a venom spider triggers a regional respawn over the next 90 minutes.
They inject a slow-acting venom that ticks damage over 60 seconds. Antidote potions must be pre-stocked; the venom is not curable in-combat by regular healing.

Their webbing is unbreakable by normal means. The only reliable way to cut through a venom-spider web is with a weapon whose reagent includes venom-spider silk — a loop that encourages repeated hunts.
monsters.reagent_callout: Treasonous ring (1/48 collection-log) — reagent for the Wilds ring of venom-resistance.

monsters.name: Vet'ion
bible: Vet'ion is a Wilds singleton boss — a skeletal mage-lord whose hellhound pack accompanies him at all times. The pack respawns faster than he does; killing the pack is a phase of the fight, not a separate encounter.
He phases at 50% HP, transforming from a single humanoid to a multi-skull form. Each head has a different attack style, forcing constant prayer switches.
Only killable with a skull on (PvP-flagged). This is a formal lore-mechanic enforcing the fight's wilderness-coded risk.
monsters.reagent_callout: Skull sceptre (1/128 collection-log) — PvP utility item (teleports player to Wilds edge once per day).

monsters.name: Callisto
monsters.examine: Bear. Immense. Reminds you why your grandfather did not go north.
bible: Callisto is the Wilds' primary melee boss, a bear-like apex that hunts in the Carrallangar area. She is enormous — roughly the mass of three ordinary bears — and her fur is scarred from decades of Wilds combat.

She attacks with swipes that cleave through armor and have a knockback effect. Her roar, triggered at 50% HP, forces all nearby players to their knees for a full combat round — potentially fatal in a PvP context.
She is treated by the Wilds fishermen as a folk-hero. Several songs about her exist; all of them warn the listener to stay south of the Wall.
monsters.reagent_callout: Dragon pickaxe (1/256 collection-log) — classic wilderness unique, fastest mining tool with special attack.

monsters.name: Frost drake
monsters.examine: A dragon-kin adapted to the cold north.
bible: Frost drakes occupy the northern Wilds, particularly the frost-touched zones where the temperature drops below freezing even in summer. They are smaller than typical dragons, breath-weapon only, and their frost-breath freezes a target in place for a combat tick.
Their scales are superlatively cold-resistant — a key material for cold-region gear crafting in Moryskah.
They hunt in pairs: a drake and its nesting-partner. Engaging one always draws the other within 20 seconds.
monsters.habitat: the Frost-Touched Zones, northern wilderness level 35+
monsters.reagent_callout: Frost-drake scale (1/16) — reagent for cold-resistance boots (Moryskah winter-crossing tier).

monsters.name: PvP hound (revenant)
monsters.examine: A hound that learned from the hunters.
bible: PvP hounds are revenant dogs that have adapted to wilderness-PvP conditions over long exposure. They recognise skulled (PvP-flagged) players and prioritise them as targets — a hound will walk past an unflagged player to reach a skull.
They drop mid-tier revenant materials as a consolation to solo players frustrated by PvP harassment.
They pack in threes, which makes them a useful training mob for small groups practicing coordinated combat.
monsters.anti_pattern_note: skull-priority aggro is real. Unflagged player should be safe in proximity.

monsters.name: Chaos fanatic
monsters.examine: A mage who stared into the Chaos Elemental and did not look away.
bible: Chaos fanatics are former Heartlands magi who travelled to the Wilds to witness the Chaos Elemental and returned changed. Each fanatic has a different physical manifestation of chaos-corruption — flickering skin, extra limbs, voices from elsewhere.
They cast chaotic spells (random from a pool of six) and cannot be prayed against reliably.
Their drop pool is chaos-themed; ancient staffs, chaos-imprinted runes, and rarely the Odium charm.
monsters.habitat: scattered Wilds ritual sites, specifically the six Chaos Shrines
monsters.reagent_callout: Odium shard (1/96) — reagent for Odium Ward (magic defence shield).

monsters.name: Scorpia
monsters.examine: A giant scorpion of the deep Wilds. Spawns offspring mid-fight.
bible: Scorpia is a Wilds singleton boss with a specific gimmick: she spawns three scorplet offspring at regular intervals during the fight. The scorplets must be killed before they grow; a grown scorplet becomes a secondary Scorpia-adjacent threat.
She is found in Scorpia's Cave, a specific deep-wilderness cave. The cave is PvP-enabled.
She drops the malediction shard; three malediction shards combine into the Malediction ward (magic-class offhand).
monsters.reagent_callout: Malediction shard (1/12 always, 3 to complete Malediction ward).
